newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech oil refinery fire near German border.
newsitem.headline: Czech oil refinery fire near German border.

text.p: An explosion ripped through a Czech oil refinery on Saturday, starting a fire visible for several kilometres (milea) away which sent dense smoke rolling into neighbouring Germany.

Three firemen were hurt as burning petrol poured from storage tanks at the Litvinov refinery, which is partly owned by an international oil consortium. Production was shut down, a spokesman for owner Ceska Rafinerska a.s. said.
Eyewitnesses said the blaze was near ammonia tanks belonging to a petrochemical complex on the same site.
The refinery's owner, Ceska Rafinerska a.s., said it would not be necessary to use state crude reserves despite the indefinite closure of one of the country's two main refineries.

Ceska Rafinerska spokesman Ales Soukup said officials from his company's parent firm Unipetrol a.s., distributors Cepro a.s. and Benzina a.s. and the Industry and Trade Ministry had calculated that supplies would be adequate for the short-term.
Soukrup said in a statement that the decision had been taken after a reveiw of supplies at Cepro and Benzina and Litvinov's sister refinery at Kralupy.
At the height of the blaze, flames were visible for dozens of kilometres around the refinery, which lies about eight km (five miles) from the border of the former East Germany.

Winds blew smoke billowing from the blaze into the German state of Saxony. The city of Dresden lies about 50 km (30 miles) north of the refinery and Czech news agency CTK reported that Czech authorities had warned their German counterparts.
"The processing refinery has been closed down," Ceska's Soukup told Reuters earlier in the day. "But there is no damage to the unit," he said.
"It has been possible to stop the main part of the leak of fuel on to the site of the fire," he said. "However, fuel is still flowing from two storage tanks and the fuel is burning."
Production would be stepped up at the Czech Republic's other major refinery at Kralupy, north of Prague.
Soukup declined comment on the ammonia tanks which belong to Czech petrochemical company Chemopetrol a.s.

By late morning, about 25 fire crews fought the blaze, pouring foam on to flames shooting some 50 metres (150 feet) into the sky and hosing down nearby petrol storage tanks in an attempt to stop the fire from spreading.
The blaze broke out in a pumping station, apparently after an explosion, and at one point directly threatened eight petrol tanks holding more than 10,000 tonnes of petrol.

In a deal completed in February this year, the IOC consortium of three foreign oil groups bought a 49 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska a.s., a company set up to operate the two oil refineries at Litvinov and Kralupy.
IOC, which is equally owned by Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco of the United States, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip SpA, paid $173 million in cash.
